blurb: Morgan Stanley Investment Management launched spot Ethereum and Solana ETPs on NYSE Arca under tickers MSSE and MSOL, each charging a 0.14% expense ratio and staking a portion of holdings while passing all rewards to investors. The staking-from-day-one design and floor-level fee push the first bank-affiliated crypto ETP franchise ahead of incumbents, extending a digital-asset suite that now spans the three largest crypto assets after the firm's earlier Bitcoin trust.

title: 10 European Banks Launch RL1 Blockchain Cooperative
blurb: Ten European financial institutions, including ABN AMRO, DZ BANK and Natixis CIB, launched Regulated Layer One, a jointly owned, permissioned blockchain for digital bond issuance, tokenized real-world assets, and repo and derivatives margining, domiciled in Luxembourg as a cooperative with one vote per member. The network, built on SWIAT's BaFin-supervised infrastructure, has run in production for three years and settled over 700 million euros ($815M) across regulated financial markets.

title: Software Woes Push Europe Lenders to Seek Rare Repayment Terms
blurb: European lenders are demanding rapid-amortization and stricter repayment terms on loans to software companies, structures rarely used since the 2008 financial crisis, on fears that AI will erode those firms' revenue. The shift signals that credit markets now price generative AI as a direct threat to software business models, raising borrowing costs for a sector that has long enjoyed cheap, covenant-light debt.

title: SoFi Says SoFiUSD Settlement Now Live on Q2 Earnings Call
blurb: SoFi confirmed on its Q2 earnings call that commercial clients are now settling transactions in real time through SoFiUSD, moving the stablecoin from launch to a live production rail seven months after SoFi became the first nationally chartered US bank to issue a stablecoin on a public blockchain. The enterprise-focused rail runs 24/7 through the SoFi Exchange Network and is slated to plug into Mastercard's global payments network.

title: PayPal turned down $53bn, and pointed to a beat and a $70 target
blurb: PayPal publicly rejected Stripe and Advent's $60.50-a-share bid, roughly $53bn, on its Q2 earnings call, where CEO Enrique Lores said the offer failed to clear its bar for shareholder value and pointed to Cantor's $70 valuation against a stock near $58. The rebuff rode a beat, with revenue up 5% to $8.68bn and raised full-year guidance, though transaction-margin dollars grew just 1% as easing rates cut interest on customer balances.

title: BNY targets $8.6 trillion transfer agency market on blockchain rails
blurb: BNY is moving its transfer agency record-keeping, which services roughly $8.6T across 7.6M accounts, onto blockchain to create a single on-chain ownership ledger for tokenized funds and cut out intermediaries. Baillie Gifford, BlackRock, and BNY's Dreyfus unit are the first clients, though the 242-year-old custodian expects traditional rails to coexist for years given cyber and smart-contract risks.

title: BlackRock Takes 80% of Meta's $14 Billion El Paso AI Data Center
blurb: Meta sold an 80% stake in its $14B El Paso AI data center to BlackRock-managed funds while staying on as sole tenant and operator, contributing $2.3B in land and construction assets against BlackRock's $4.9B in cash. The structure leans on Meta residual value guarantees with a ~$13B threshold, and the deal's ~$12.5B bond sale cleared only after weak demand pushed investment-grade yields toward junk-rated levels.

title: Tether’s GENIUS-compliant USAT stablecoin launches on Celo, marking first expansion beyond Ethereum
blurb: Tether launched USAT, its GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoin issued by OCC-chartered Anchorage Digital Bank, on Celo, its first mainnet deployment beyond Ethereum since going live in January. Celo's CIP-64 fee abstraction lets users pay gas directly in USAT rather than holding CELO, and the network already handles 28% of cross-chain USDT transfers, giving Tether's regulated dollar a high-volume distribution base.

title: MoonPay launches PayBox, an AI payment vault for ChatGPT and Claude
blurb: MoonPay launched PayBox, a non-custodial payment vault that connects to ChatGPT and Claude, letting the assistant prepare transactions like flight bookings and restaurant reservations that users approve with a passkey before funds move. Built on the x402 agent-payment standard now backed by Visa, Mastercard, and Stripe, PayBox combines crypto wallets and cards across Solana and EVM chains, with an autonomous mode for spending within user-set limits.

title: BMO Completes SRTs Tied to $5 Billion of Corporate Loans
blurb: Bank of Montreal completed two significant risk transfers covering roughly $5 billion of corporate loans, joining a growing list of Canadian lenders using SRTs to offload credit risk and free up regulatory capital. The trades tap heavy investor appetite for the instruments, which let banks keep loans on their books while shifting first-loss exposure to funds hunting yield.

title: SoFi crypto transaction revenue grows 10% to $134 million in Q2
blurb: SoFi's crypto transaction revenue grew 10% quarter over quarter to $134.3M in Q2, though after $133.1M in transaction costs it netted just $1.2M, up from roughly $850K in Q1. The bigger signal is SoFiUSD moving from consumer app into commercial payments, with the company's Big Business Banking platform now settling round-the-clock transactions on the SoFi Exchange Network for enterprise clients.

title: LemonEdge raises £15.8m to modernise private market infrastructure
blurb: LemonEdge raised $21M (£15.8m) Series A led by Blackstone Innovations Investments to modernize fund accounting for private markets, with BNY participating.

title: Stablecoin firm Brale says new protocol can remove a major hurdle to scaling custom tokens
blurb: Brale introduced ION Protocol on testnet, an interoperability system that moves participating stablecoins across blockchains by burning tokens on one chain and minting them on another, without the pre-funded liquidity pools most bridges require. The launch targets fragmentation in a stablecoin market that now spans more than 350 tokens and over $300B in market cap, cutting the capital issuers must lock up on every supported chain.

title: CDS Market Surges as Wall Street Picks AI’s Winners and Losers
blurb: The credit-default-swap market is repricing AI risk as Big Tech's planned trillions in capex strain a key corner of credit markets, lifting the cost of financing data centers and chips. Rising CDS spreads on the heaviest AI spenders give lenders and investors an early read on which hyperscalers and infrastructure bets Wall Street expects to pay off and which it now views as exposed.

title: Visa Beats Estimates, Takes $563 Million Charge on Job Cuts
blurb: Visa reported fiscal Q3 profit that beat Wall Street estimates, hours after telling staff it will cut roughly 2,600 jobs and take a $563M charge. The reductions at the world's largest payments network signal a push to control costs even as transaction volumes hold up, testing whether headcount cuts can coexist with continued network growth.

title: Elon Musk finally launches X Money. What could possibly go wrong?
blurb: X Money launched Monday for US Premium and Premium+ subscribers, offering peer-to-peer payments and a 6% yield, but it lacks money transmitter licenses in New York and Massachusetts and restricts P2P transfers to other X Money users over 18. The licensing gaps mean the X Card can't be used everywhere through Google Pay or Apple Pay, and payments experts warn that inconsistent acceptance will create enough friction to stall mainstream adoption.
